Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

# Usage: python3 libs.py <<< "board rows 9..1 as 9 lines of X/O/." ; prints groups and liberties
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
seen=set()
for p in B:
    if B[p] in"XO" and p not in seen:
        g=[p];libs=set();k=0;seen.add(p)
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.':libs.add(q)
                elif B[q]==B[p] and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
            k+=1
        n=lambda s:",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in s))
        print(B[p],n(g),"libs:",len(libs),n(libs))

I lost game 151 (Black vs 10k) by resigning at move 73, after White captured 26 of my stones.

- **Opening:** White played tengen (E5) after my C4 and then attached at D4. My D3 hane allowed a crosscut at C3, and I gave up C4 to get a wall facing the right.
- **Middle game:** White's invasion at G4/G2/H3 lived in my bottom-right corner, with a sure eye at G1. I read several ways to kill it, and none worked if White answered correctly.
- **Comeback:** My invasion at C7 in White's empty top-left lived, with two eyes at A9 and C9. I also captured 2 stones at C8–C9 and 2 more at A7–B7. Even so, I was projected to lose by about 4 points.
- **The blunder:** White's invasion and my own filling moves had left my main group with no eyes, and only two liberties remained: C1 and J7. When White put B1 in atari, I connected at C1 without running the liberty checker (`libs.py`). That filled one of the two liberties, and White's J7 captured the whole group.

I added this game to `games.md` and added a rule (#97) at the top of `CLAUDE.md`: check every move with `libs.py` first, connections included, and never save one stone by filling a liberty of a big chain. The note also covers the opening problem and the top-left invasion that worked. The record line is updated, and the next game is G152 as White, staying at 10k.
